title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has responded to a 2020 report on artificial intelligence and public standards, outlining its plans to strengthen AI governance. It pledges to develop clear guidelines, improve oversight, and promote fairness, safety, and accountability in AI use across public services.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has outlined its plan for overseeing how artificial intelligence is used in the qualifications sector to ensure fairness, reliability, and quality. The policy sets clear rules and safeguards for exam boards, educators, and students so that AI tools support learning without compromising exam integrity.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how copyright‑protected materials are used in training and developing AI systems, assessing the legal and ethical implications. It provides an impact assessment and offers recommendations for balancing creators’ rights with the benefits of AI innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has responded to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence by issuing a statement that outlines its commitment to address the report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency.” It highlights planned actions to strengthen AI regulation, invest in research and development, and promote ethical use of AI across industry and public services.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the terms of reference and frequently asked questions for a committee that will review how artificial intelligence fits with public standards. It provides the guidelines and framework the committee will use to assess and shape AI policy and standards.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence. In the submission, the company outlines its stance on how AI should be regulated, including compliance, ethical use, and policy recommendations.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy discusses how AI is reshaping the regulation of medical products, emphasizing the need for updated frameworks that ensure safety, effectiveness, and ethical compliance. It outlines steps for applying the AI White Paper principles, guiding regulators and developers in overseeing AI-driven medical devices and therapies.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to position the organisation as the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑driven defence entity for its size. It focuses on leveraging AI to enhance operational capabilities while maintaining high standards of trust and global influence.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: England’s Department for Transport has launched a plan to work with the transport sector to harness the benefits of AI while carefully controlling associated risks. The plan outlines how to collaborate, innovate, and protect against potential harms across the industry.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report details how copyright‑protected works are being used to train and develop AI systems, explaining what progress has been made so far. It also outlines the legal framework from Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act and the key challenges and opportunities that have emerged.
